chapters.title: The Loop That Lies to Itself
chapters.blurb: A builder and a critic can volley forever: every attempt plausible, every refutation fair, and nobody watching the trajectory. Plot the verdicts and the failure appears — an orbit that never approaches zero.

chapters.title: Rounds of Three, and the Judge
chapters.blurb: Rework runs in rounds of three, and at attempts three, six, and nine a third critic convenes: the progress judge reads the successive verdicts, oldest first, and rules on exactly one question — is this converging?

chapters.title: Thrash, the Cap, and the Loud Stop
chapters.blurb: Two refutations with the identical finding set are a proof, not an opinion — no judge needed. Ten attempts is the hard cap. And every stop flips the project to invalid loop: written, committed, loud.

chapters.title: When to Stop Honestly
chapters.blurb: An unbounded loop turns failure into spend; a bare cap kills work one round from landing. The judge is what lets the cap be generous — and stopping honestly is what earns the right to run unattended.
